source.paper: Ellis–Schmidt (Gen. Rel. Grav. 8 (1977)), as quoted by Hörmann
source.statement: "there can be no global Cauchy surfaces in these space-times" (the conical spacetime with the singular set deleted)
the initial value surface then cannot be a Cauchy hypersurface in the classical sense (points of non-smoothness deleted)

hypotheses.paper: the axis removed (target: the restriction of the causality to regPart α, an open set)
hypotheses.note: massive α read on the open set regOpens α = ℝ × (C_α \ {apex}) (kb/0001): IsCauchySurfaceOn, GloballyHyperbolicOn; curves and their extensions inside reg. coe_regOpens : (regOpens α : Set _) = regPart α by rfl
any subset of any slice {t = t₀} (not_isCauchySurfaceOn_regOpens_of_subset_slice), and in fact no subset of reg at all (not_exists_isCauchySurfaceOn_regOpens)
the witness massive_infall t₀ is chronal on every segment (uniformly timelike, speed 1/2), so the slice fails for timelike curves as well

findings: The target's (2) holds in a much stronger form: reg(E_α) admits NO Cauchy surface whatsoever (not_exists_isCauchySurfaceOn_regOpens), which is exactly Ellis–Schmidt's claim (hormann2015conical.txt:500-501), and reg(E_α) is not globally hyperbolic (not_globallyHyperbolicOn_regOpens: the diamond from (−2, r=1) to (2, r=1) on one ray is not closed in reg). The roadmap title and SYNTHESIS.md:100 ('with the axis removed it is not') may be strengthened to 'with the axis removed there is none'.

The proof of 'no Cauchy surface' is a three-curve argument on one radial half-plane, valid in any static ℝ × X with the cylinder ℝ × A over a closed A reached by a 1-Lipschitz ray removed (staticCausality.IsRayTo.not_exists_isCauchySurfaceOn): the null ray into A at time 0 meets S at time τ₂ < 0, the null ray into A at time 3τ₂ meets S at τ₁ < 3τ₂, and the curve along the second ray, out along an outgoing null ray, then in along the first, is inextensible and meets S twice. No smooth Geroch theorem is used.
E_α is globally hyperbolic while its open subset reg(E_α) is not: GH does not pass to open subsets, witnessed on a model (massive_globallyHyperbolic, not_globallyHyperbolicOn_regOpens).
questions: Ellis–Schmidt's sentence is known here only through Hörmann's quotation (hormann2015conical.txt:500-501); the 1977 paper is not archived. The Lean statement is the ETT reading: no subset of reg(E_α) is met exactly once by every inextensible causal curve of reg(E_α) (DEC-14).

source.statement: Q4 #4: In E_α × ℝ, {t=0} is Cauchy for all α > 0; with the axis removed it is not; explicit J⁻(x) ∩ {t=0} through axis points
for a point x on the axis, the past null cone Ĉ0−(x) is given in quasi-Cartesian coordinates by the usual Minkowskian formula
the solution at x depends not just on the initial data on C0−(x) ∩ S but also on points in C0−(ξ) ∩ S with ξ ∈ C0−(x) ∩ Λ

hypotheses.note: x = (t₀, apex) (2+1), x = (t₀, (apex, z₀)) (3+1); the general formula holds for every x: J⁻(x) ∩ {t = t₁} = {t₁} × closedBall x.2 (x.1 − t₁), J⁺ likewise, both compact

hypotheses.paper: the past null cone (Vickers–Wilson) vs the causal past (target)
hypotheses.note: both: J⁻(x) ∩ {t = 0} = {r ≤ t₀} and (J⁻ \ I⁻)(x) ∩ {t = 0} = {r = t₀}; 3+1: r² + (z − z₀)² ≤ t₀² (resp. = t₀²), with t₀ ≥ 0

findings: Vickers–Wilson's 'usual Minkowskian formula' for an axis point holds exactly, for every cone angle α > 0 and for the causal past as well as the null cone. Their non-sharpness remark has an exact causal counterpart: J⁻(x) = J⁻_reg(x) ∪ ⋃_{ξ ∈ J⁻(x) ∩ axis} J⁻(ξ) (massive_Jminus_eq_reg_union_axis), every causal curve to x either avoids the axis or passes through an axis point ξ ≤ x.
questions: 'J⁻(x) ∩ {t=0} through axis points' (SYNTHESIS.md:100) is read as: x on the axis. The formula for every x and the decomposition of J⁻(x) through the axis points it contains are proved as well, so no other reading is left unproved. Whether the second part of the decomposition is ever needed off the axis (points of reg in J⁻(x) reached only through the apex; expected for α > 2π, where the apex lies on minimising geodesics between directions ≥ π apart, and not for α < 2π) is not settled here.

kb_proposals: A static spacetime ℝ × X with the timelike cylinder ℝ × A over a closed A removed, A reached by a 1-Lipschitz ray (staticCausality.IsRayTo), has no Cauchy surface and is not globally hyperbolic on that open set (IsRayTo.not_exists_isCauchySurfaceOn, .not_globallyHyperbolicOn): cheap non-GH, non-Cauchy open subsets of GH models, e.g. reg(E_α), Minkowski minus a line (T-loc-ealpha-cauchy).

A causal curve of an open W over ]-∞, b[ that tends to a point outside W at b, with a ≤_W-monotone function unbounded below along it, is inextensible in W: Causality.inextensible_Iio_of_tendsto_not_mem (model-free; the 'curve runs into the boundary' pattern). Hoist candidate to the ETT layer (kb/0047).

Every slice {t = t₀} of a static spacetime over a complete geodesic space is a Cauchy surface: staticCausality.isCauchySurface_slice (Geroch (ii)⇒(iii) with t − t₀); the generic static side conditions (chronalNeighbours, causallyOpen, stronglyCausalOpen, hasTimeFunction, noCausalEndpoint) are in CausalScaffold.EAlphaCauchy.

Hörmann's 3+1 conical spacetime is cosmicString α = staticCausality (WithLp 2 (Cone α × ℝ)); WithLp 2 products of geodesic/proper metric spaces are geodesic/proper (instances GeodesicSpace.withLpTwo, properSpace_withLpTwo), WithLp.fst/snd need no group structure, and withLp_dist_two gives the √(d₁² + d₂²) formula. Hörmann's α_H is α/2π.
